A1.justification: Both complete 32-page PDFs describe SWE-Search and contain matching main sections, references, and Appendices A-L. Text, equations, tables, and graphical content support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v3 reports original SWE-bench Lite experiments across five models, including resolve rates in Table 1, search and selection analyses, and supplementary results in the appendices.

after.justification: v4 retains these original experiments and appendix analyses, including the resolve rates in Table 1 and compute-matched comparisons in Table 4.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same flexible Action Agent, modified MCTS selection procedure, quantitative and qualitative Value Agent feedback, and discriminator debate. The appendix prompts are also unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same SWE-bench Lite software-issue tasks. The repository coverage and supplementary evaluation scenarios in the appendices are unchanged.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains Moatless-v0.0.2 and Moatless-Adapted in the same comparisons. Appendix J and Table 4 retain the same compute-matched Moatless-Adapted comparisons.

E3.justification: The 300-instance evaluation, Pass@1 and Pass@5 metrics, model configurations, and reported search budgets are unchanged. Appendix J also retains the same candidate-generation and compute-matching protocol.

E4.justification: The hindsight-feedback case study, state-specific prompt comparison, search-scaling analysis, and discriminator comparison are retained. Appendices D-F and I-J contain the same loop-avoidance, model-complementarity, value-function, cost, and compute-matching analyses.

E5.justification: Figure 8 retains the same standard-deviation error bars. Appendix J retains its description of five candidates from one SWE-Search run versus five Moatless-Adapted runs; no statistical reporting is added or revised.

E6.justification: All numerical entries and graphical results are unchanged. For example, Table 1 reports GPT-4o resolve rates of 31.0 for SWE-Search and 25.7 for Moatless-Adapted in both versions; appendix costs and compute-matched results also match.

T1.justification: Section 3.1 retains the same formal problem formulation and history-dependent value description. Equations 1-4, including the modified UCT criterion, are unchanged, with no added or revised proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions and scientific claims, including the claimed 23% relative improvement across five models and performance scaling with additional search.

C2.justification: Interpretations concerning feedback, state-specific evaluation, complementary model strengths, and imperfect final-solution selection are unchanged. The computational-cost discussion and proposed applicability extensions are also retained.

D1.justification: Implementation details, MCTS hyperparameters, test-execution descriptions, and value/discriminator prompts are identical. Code and demo links, reproducibility statements, and release wording are unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2 and the reference list contain the same cited works. The positioning relative to existing search methods, software agents, and multi-agent debate remains unchanged.

P1.justification: The running header changes from 'Preprint.' to 'Published as a conference paper at ICLR 2025.' The first-page arXiv stamp updates from v3/15 Dec 2024 to v4/17 Feb 2025. Body prose and section structure are unchanged.

P2.justification: The first page has small vertical-spacing adjustments around the author block, abstract, and introduction. All figures, tables, captions, and their placements remain unchanged; subsequent page bodies visually match.

improvement.justification: v4 updates publication-status text and slightly adjusts first-page spacing. The methods, evidence, claims, explanations, and reproducibility information remain identical throughout the main text and appendices, establishing no meaningful overall quality difference.
